finalAnswer:
I added the 2014 Arctic-country electricity-use layer to the map.

Among known rows, Iceland is highest at 53,832.5 kWh per capita. Canada and Finland are also high, while Denmark and Russia are lowest among the known values. The legend uses five quantile classes with breaks at 7,865.6, 13,188.4, 14,542.1, and 15,522.0 kWh per capita, plus a neutral No data category.

There are 7 known country features and 1 No data feature. The retained Norway benchmark row stayed No data because its supplied ISO_A3 value is `-99`, so it could not exactly match the frozen World Bank `Country Code` field.

This is a fixed 2014 country-level benchmark, not current consumption and not a subnational map.
